title: The Product of a Range Modulo 1000000007, With Changes

concept.title: Multiplication modulo a prime is associative, so the tree works; division is not needed
body: A row of numbers changes one cell at a time, and a question asks for the **product of the numbers from `x` to `y`**, written modulo `1000000007` (a prime, and the usual modulus for big answers). For `2 3 4` the product of all three is 24. The real product of 30000 numbers up to 10^9 has hundreds of thousands of digits, so it is always taken modulo the prime.

It is tempting to use a table of prefix products and divide, as for prefix sums: `product(x..y) = P[y] / P[x - 1]`. Division modulo a prime is possible (with a modular inverse), but after a change the whole table from that cell on would have to be rebuilt, and the numbers can be a multiple of the prime in other problems. A segment tree avoids both issues: **multiplication modulo the prime is associative** with the neutral element 1, so the tree is the one used for sums, with `a * b % MOD` instead of `a + b`.

body.code:
MOD = 1000000007
tree[size + i] = a[i] % MOD; unused leaves = 1
for v in range(size - 1, 0, -1): tree[v] = tree[2*v] * tree[2*v + 1] % MOD
# a change sets a leaf and recomputes the parents; a question multiplies the blocks of the range modulo MOD

body: Every multiplication stays below `MOD^2 = 10^18`, which fits in a signed 64-bit integer, so no special arithmetic is needed in C++ and Java. Each operation costs O(log n) modular multiplications. In the real contest practice this pattern is used for products, for counting ways and for polynomial hashes of ranges.

statement: A row of `n` positive numbers is given. Process `q` operations: type 1 `x y` sets the number at the position `x` to `y`; type 2 `x y` asks for the product of the numbers at the positions `x` to `y`, modulo 1000000007. Print the answers to the questions on one line, in order.
inputFormat: The first line has `n` and `q`: the number of cells and the number of operations.
The second line has `n` numbers: the cells.
Each of the next `q` lines has three numbers `t`, `x` and `y`. If `t = 1`, set the cell number `x` to the value `y`. If `t = 2`, print the product of the cells `x` to `y` modulo 1000000007.
outputFormat: Print one number for every operation of type 2, separated by spaces.
constraints: Cells are numbered from 1; for a question 1 <= x <= y <= n.
hints: Use the sum tree with multiplication modulo 1000000007 instead of addition.
A product of two residues fits in 64 bits.

explanation: Multiplication modulo the prime is associative with neutral element 1, so a segment tree of products supports changes and range products in O(log n) multiplications.
solution.complexity: Time O((n + q) log n), space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, q = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
ops = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(q)]

mod = 1000000007
size = 1
while size < n:
    size *= 2
tree = [1] * (2 * size)
for i in range(n):
    tree[size + i] = a[i] % mod
for v in range(size - 1, 0, -1):
    tree[v] = tree[2 * v] * tree[2 * v + 1] % mod
out = []
for kind, x, y in ops:
    if kind == 1:
        v = size + x - 1
        tree[v] = y % mod
        v //= 2
        while v:
            tree[v] = tree[2 * v] * tree[2 * v + 1] % mod
            v //= 2
    else:
        lo = size + x - 1
        hi = size + y
        res = 1
        while lo < hi:
            if lo & 1:
                res = res * tree[lo] % mod
                lo += 1
            if hi & 1:
                hi -= 1
                res = res * tree[hi] % mod
            lo //= 2
            hi //= 2
        out.append(res)
print(*out)
